title: House and Well
premise: Astrid Brightwater, a meticulous urban explorer, discovers unmapped tunnels beneath the old Brightwater house and learns the founders built it as a machine for harvesting identity — every mirror in the house reflects one second late because the reflections are being siphoned into the well below. As the lag widens, Astrid's own reflection begins acting independently, committing small cruelties that the town blames on them. To survive, Astrid must complete the founders' interrupted ritual before the harvest moon rises — but finishing it means choosing who gets erased: themselves, or everyone whose faces float in the well. In the end, Astrid shatters the ritual's keystone mirror, drowning the harvested selves back into the earth, and walks out of the house as someone no mirror will ever quite recognize again.
about_author: Rosalind Nystrom is a former building surveyor from coastal Maine who spent a decade documenting condemned properties before turning to fiction. She writes horror about architecture that remembers, and claims she has never lived in a house she didn't first measure herself.

chapters.title: The Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Establishes their ritualized habits: photographing doorways, counting exits, mapping the Brightwater house's cellar on a whim. They find a stairwell behind plaster that appears on no survey. Emotional beat: quiet competence curdling into unease when the count of doors comes out wrong twice.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The bathroom mirror reflects their raised hand a beat after they move it. They test it with a metronome app; the lag is exactly 1.0 seconds and growing. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery giving way to the specific dread of something watching patiently.

chapters.title: The Well Below
chapters.summary: Astrid descends the hidden stair and finds a dry stone well ringed with mirrors angled inward, all reflecting a room that isn't there. Faces flicker in the waterless dark. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation — this place was built to be found by someone like them.

chapters.title: Founder's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, intercut with ledger excerpts. In the town archive they find the Brightwater founders' accounts: payments for 'glass,' 'silence,' and 'the keeping of names.' The last entry is unfinished. Emotional beat: scholarly fascination shadowed by the realization the ritual was interrupted mid-sentence.

chapters.title: What My Hands Did
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Their reflection acts during the lagged second — knocking a cup, scratching words into fog. Neighbors mention seeing Astrid somewhere they weren't. Emotional beat: the horror of being framed by yourself, of justice arriving without trial.

chapters.title: Deputy Vane
chapters.summary: Deputy Vane's POV. She investigates complaints against Astrid and finds the evidence too neat, too curated — someone wants Astrid blamed. Her own reflection hesitates at her window. Emotional beat: an outsider's suspicion becoming reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Harvest Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Deciphers the ledger: the ritual completes under the harvest moon, twelve days away, and requires a living keeper to finish it. The lag reaches two seconds. Emotional beat: a countdown beginning, time itself complicit.

chapters.title: The Second Astrid
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Their reflection steps fully free during a blackout and speaks with their voice, offering partnership: finish the ritual together and neither of them gets erased. Emotional beat: temptation — power offered by the self you distrust most.

chapters.title: Names in the Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the well they see the harvested: generations of townsfolk, including children listed as 'gone missing' in old papers. The founders fed it deliberately. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into fury — this was never haunting, it was policy.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. She admits her family name is in the well; her great-aunt was 'kept' in 1954. She agrees to help Astrid, breaking procedure she's spent her life upholding. Emotional beat: choosing justice outside the law when the law was founded on the crime.

chapters.title: The House Rearranges
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Corridors lengthen, doors migrate overnight, and the counted doors now number thirteen. The house is preparing the ritual space. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the mapmaker losing the map.

chapters.title: Keystone
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They identify the keystone mirror in the well chamber — the first glass, which holds the founders' original bargain. Breaking it should collapse the harvest. But the reflection warns it will take Astrid down too. Emotional beat: weighing self against principle.

chapters.title: Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. At a public hearing about Astrid's alleged crimes, mirrors in the courthouse lag visibly; half the town sees their doubles and goes silent with recognition. Emotional beat: collective denial cracking — complicity exposed in real time.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Glass
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The reflection offers a final deal: let the ritual finish, keep your body, rule what remains. Astrid refuses and the reflection takes hostages — Vane's image freezes mid-blink. Emotional beat: the cost of refusal made flesh.

chapters.title: Three Days Dark
chapters.summary: Astrid and Vane cover every mirror in the house with black cloth, buying time. The cloth sweats and breathes. The lag spreads to windows, to still water, to Vane's phone screen. Emotional beat: siege mentality, tenderness between allies under pressure.

chapters.title: The Founder's Heir
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They trace the ledger to a living descendant, old Mrs. Aldous, who reveals the ritual needs a willing heir — and Astrid's bloodline qualifies through a branch nobody recorded. Emotional beat: identity destabilized; the enemy was always family.

chapters.title: Moonrise Preparations
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The house uncovers its own mirrors; the well fills with light though there is no water. Vane guards the stairwell while Astrid prepares to descend. Emotional beat: grim resolve before the storm.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They enter the well chamber as the moon crests, surrounded by every harvested face calling them by name — including their mother's. The reflection waits at the keystone with a hammer, offering to break it if Astrid only says yes to the ritual first. Emotional beat: the trap's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: The Ritual Completed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Forced to choose, Astrid speaks the founders' closing words but substitutes their own name for the required sacrifice, binding the harvest to themselves alone. The keystone cracks. Emotional beat: self-erasure as the ultimate act of justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The house convulses; mirrors burst in sequence like gunfire. Vane drags a hollow-eyed Astrid up the migrating stairs as the well drinks itself dry. Emotional beat: desperate loyalty against collapsing architecture.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unmirrored
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Charges dissolve as the planted evidence unravels with the house's power. Astrid returns to find the cellar sealed in raw stone, no stair, no well. Their reflection in a shop window moves perfectly — but doesn't look quite like them anymore. Emotional beat: survival with permanent alteration.

chapters.title: House and Well
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Astrid's POV. Months later, Astrid publishes the maps anonymously and visits the sealed site each equinox, leaving flowers for the names in the ledger. In the last line, a puddle outside the house lags one second — then catches up. Emotional beat: vigilance as peace; some houses are never finished with you.
